title: A field theory approach to Breit-type Hamiltonians in gapped Dirac systems
authors: Xinhong Zhou, T. H. Hansson, Varsha Subramanyan, Qing-Dong Jiang
abstract: We develop a path-integral-based field theory for deriving Breit-type low-energy Hamiltonians for gapped Dirac systems coupled to both vector and axial gauge fields. Treating the mass gap as the large energy scale, we integrate out the high-energy component of the Dirac spinor and obtain a canonical Schrödinger description for the remaining low-energy degrees of freedom. For the ordinary Dirac equation, our method reproduces the conventional Breit Hamiltonian order by order. In the presence of axial gauge fields, however, the resulting Hamiltonian contains additional vector-axial couplings that have no analogue in the traditional electromagnetic case. We illustrate the method using three- and two-dimensional Dirac models and discuss its relevance to gapped Weyl systems, where dynamical axial fields can generate distinctive low-energy transport signatures.
summary: This work presents a systematic field theory method to derive effective Breit-type Hamiltonians for gapped Dirac systems interacting with both vector and axial gauge fields. By integrating out high-energy degrees of freedom, the authors establish a canonical low-energy description. The key finding is that axial couplings introduce unique terms into the Hamiltonian not found in standard electromagnetism.
main_problem: The paper develops a field theory approach to derive effective, low-energy Breit-type Hamiltonians for gapped Dirac systems coupled to both vector and axial gauge fields.
main_result: It shows that while the method reproduces standard results for ordinary Dirac equations, the inclusion of axial fields introduces novel vector-axial couplings into the resulting Hamiltonian.
method: The authors use a path-integral formalism, integrating out high-energy components of the Dirac spinor and expanding in inverse powers of the mass gap to obtain a canonical Schrödinger description.
model_or_system: The model involves gapped Dirac fermions coupled to external vector (A_mu) and axial (A^5_mu) gauge potentials, studied in both 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions. The effective theory is derived by treating the mass gap as the large energy scale.
key_observables: The effective Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{	ext{eff}}$), particularly the novel vector-axial coupling terms when axial fields are present, and potential Hall-type transport currents.
important_parameters: The mass gap ($m$), the external gauge potentials ($A_\mu, A^5_\mu$), and dimensionality (2D vs 3D).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that the mass gap is the large energy scale and that relevant momenta are much smaller than this gap. Field rescaling based on symplectic structure is crucial for canonical quantization.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the field theory, first deriving the effective action by integrating out high-energy modes, then performing necessary field rescalings to obtain a canonical Hamiltonian, and finally applying this procedure to specific dimensions (3+1D and 2+1D) to analyze the resulting couplings.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of low-energy Hamiltonians from continuum field theories is fundamental for understanding effective models in condensed matter physics, especially when topological or chiral symmetries are involved.
